February 27, 2025 Krysta West, Deputy Director
Good afternoon, Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker and members of the ACF Committee. My name is
Krysta West. I live in Readfield and am testifying today on behalf of the Maine Forest Products Council in support
of LD 379, "An Act to Protect Wildfire Planning and Preparedness Data."
For 65 years, the Maine Forest Products Council has served as the voice of Maine's forest economy, representing more than 300 members from all facets of the forest products industry. Our members include pulp and paper mills,
sawmills, secondary wood processors, foresters, loggers and truckers. We also represent commercial landowners
managing more than 8 million acres of forestland.
As a side note, if you would like to learn more about our members, and the il1l'lOVfl'[lV6 products they are manufacturing from Maine's forests, you are invited to join us on March l8 at our office across town for a breakfast
expo event. Legislators are welcome to come and go between 7-8:30 am. We will have products ranging from wood
fiber-based firefighting foam to drum sticks on display. There will even be a logging truck! Please join us to speak
directly with our members and to learn more about the future of the forest products industry in Maine. An invitation is attached to my testimony.
The bill before you today, LD 379, is important because it protects information necessary for the Maine Forest
Service to swiftly and effectively respond to wildfires. In Maine, 94% of the forest land is privately owned` , making access to private information essential for MFS to carry out its mission of "protecting Maine's forest resources from the effects of fire, insects, disease and misuse?" When there is a significant forest fire in Maine, loggers, truckers,
road construction operators, foresters and landowners work closely with the Maine Forest Service as a team to prevent the dangerous escalation of fires.
Information provided to the Maine Forest Service for wildfire planning and response efforts includes gate combinations, points of contact, equipment ownership information, proprietary business information and more. It also includes personal contact information for local emergency responders, contractors and land managers and proprietary information about management plans. This information, which is provided on a voluntary basis, is critical for emergency response planning purposes. Those providing that information, whether it be private landowners, municipalities, fire departments, etc., should have the assurance that this information is protected from public requests under the Freedom of Access Act. There is no reason for the public to have access to information of
this nature.
We would like to thank the Maine Forest Service for bringing this proposal forward. It highlights their commitment
to collaboration and its sensitivity to the handling of confidential information. Please vote `Ought to Pass' . Thank
you and I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.

TESTIMONY BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON AGRICULTURE, CONSERVATION AND FORESTRY

IN SUPPORT OF LD 379

An Act to Protect Wildfire Planning and Preparedness Data

February 27, 2025

Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry, my name is Robby Gross. I am the Chief Forest Ranger of the
Maine Forest Service (MFS) at the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF). I am
testifying in support of LD 379, An Act to Protect Wildfire Planning and Preparedness Data.
MFS has the final on-site authority and responsibility for controlling all wildfires in the state of Maine.
This responsibility includes formulating emergency or wildfire response plans for the safe and effective response to wildfires throughout Maine. These plans are developed and updated annually and include infonnation from public and private entities. With 92 percent of Maine land under private ownership,
MFS relies on its partnerships with landowners, land managers, contractors, and companies to ensure we
have suitable response capacity on private lands to ensure quick wildfire suppression actions. This partnership includes collecting vital information regarding land access, property use, points of contact,
and personal information that is often given to MFS for its use in emergency response planning. Examples
include gate key and lock combinations to access properties, propriety information regarding land use such as land management plans and high-value property areas, phone numbers and email addresses, and
i
equipment ownership information.
MFS is responsible for protecting this information and ensuring it is not released for other unintended
uses. This information is not currently protected by statute and is subject to the Freedom of Access Act (FOAA). This bill would provide that protection to ensure vital response information is not shared outside of emergency response planning and response without owners' consent.
The protection of Maine's forests is an immense responsibility that MFS takes very seriously. With
climate change and the threat of wildfire increasing in the Northeast, it is critical that landowners trust our ability to collect and utilize emergency response information and that this information is not
compromised. Thank you for your time. I would be happy to answer any questions now or at the work
session.

LD 379, "An Act Regarding Confidential Information Gathered for
Forest Fire Emergency Response and Planning"
Public Hearing: February 27, 2025
Sen. Talbot-Ross, Rep. Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture,
Conservation, and Forestry:
My name is Senator Russell Black and I am before you today to give you a brief introduction to LD 379, "An Act Regarding Confidential Information Gathered for Forest Fire Emergency
Response and Planning."
The Maine Forest Service is responsible for controlling wildfires in the state and creating response plans to quickly and effectively suppress fires. These plans include important information such as gate combinations, phone numbers, email addresses, land use plans, and equipment ownership details that are provided by landowners, contractors, and response teams.
Currently, this information is not protected, which means it could be accessed for purposes other than wildfire response. This could discourage people from sharing the necessary information, impacting the ability to fight fires effectively.
The goal of this bill is to protect this sensitive information while still allowing the Maine Forest
Service to respond quickly and efficiently to wildfires. By giving the Forest Service the tools to
secure this information, the bill aims to ensure both data protection and effective wildfire
response.
You will hear from members of the department who will provide additional information
regarding this bill.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
